## How to use these
Click into any code block and press **Run**. Edit the code and run it again. Lab exercises
have **Hint** and **Solution** buttons.

The first cell on a page takes a few seconds to start while Python loads. After that it is
immediate.

## About the data

Every dataset in this course is real and traces to a named public source — the
Pennsylvania Department of Health, the CDC, or the EPA. County-level figures are reported
as published, including their suppression rules and known limitations.

## Submitting a lab: needs more work. 

## Homework

Each homework is a single public-health question broken into parts, and each part
exercises something taught in that module's lecture and lab. Homework notebooks give you
the code that loads the data and nothing else — you write the rest from an empty cell.

Work in Colab, then submit the saved notebook: `File > Download > Download .ipynb`. Make
sure your outputs and figures are visible in the file you upload. **Pairs are allowed.**

## Software

Coursework is completed in [Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com). The slides on
this site run Python directly in the browser through
[Pyodide](https://pyodide.org), which requires no account and no installation.
